slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 28:12: And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down the ladder.
slides.body: “And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down the ladder.”
slides.heading: Gen 28:12

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces John's striking reuse of Jacob's ladder vision.
slides.body: Jacob sees angels ascending and descending between earth and heaven. Jesus repeats that distinctive movement—but says the angels will ascend and descend on the Son of Man.
slides.heading: Did Jacob's ladder predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents Jesus as the fulfilment of the ladder's mediating imagery.
slides.body: The verbal echo is unmistakable. John relocates the angels' movement onto the Son of Man, making Jesus central to the open-heaven scene. Christians therefore see him as the meeting point of heaven and earth.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three distinguishes John's explicit typology from Genesis's original meaning.
slides.body: Genesis reassures Jacob about God's presence, land and family. It predicts no future bridge-person. John transforms the image, and scholars debate its exact mapping. The typology is strong precisely because John makes it—not because Genesis states it.
slides.heading: Deliberate reuse, not an original forecast

title: Did Jacob's ladder predict Jesus as heaven's bridge?
